description: The toolchain that turns code into running software: Git from first commit to rebase, pull-request workflows, continuous integration, containers, automated testing and deployment, and the monitoring that tells you when to roll back. Taught to the depth of industry DevOps practice.
modelledOn: Kim, Humble, Debois and Willis, The DevOps Handbook
Beyer, Jones, Petoff and Murphy, Site Reliability Engineering
outcomes: Use Git fluently: commits, branches, merges, rebases, tags, stashes and history rewriting, and explain the object model behind them.
Collaborate through remote repositories with pull requests, code review and a branching strategy.
Resolve merge conflicts and recover from mistakes with reflog, revert and reset.
Build a continuous integration pipeline that lints, tests and packages a project on every push.
Containerise an application with Docker and compose multi-service environments.
Deploy automatically to a host, monitor it with logs and metrics, and roll back safely.

units.title: Why version control and the Git model
topics: The problem: copies of copies, lost work, who changed what; centralised versus distributed VCS
Git's object model: blobs, trees, commits, refs; the working tree, index and repository
Installing Git, configuring identity, the command line and a GUI client
Shell basics needed for the course: paths, pipes, environment variables

units.title: Git basics: commit, branch, merge
topics: init, status, add, commit; good commit messages; .gitignore
log, diff, show; inspecting history; blame
Branches as pointers; checkout and switch; fast-forward and three-way merges
Tags, stash, amend; undoing with restore, revert and reset (soft, mixed, hard)
Rebase versus merge; interactive rebase to clean history; reflog as the safety net

units.title: Remote repositories and pull requests
topics: clone, fetch, pull, push; remotes and tracking branches; SSH keys and tokens
GitHub and GitLab: issues, pull or merge requests, reviews, protected branches
Forking workflow for open source; feature-branch and trunk-based development; GitFlow compared
Code review practice: small changes, checklists, constructive comments
Semantic versioning and releases

units.title: Resolving conflicts and collaboration failures
topics: How conflicts arise; reading conflict markers; resolving in the editor and with a merge tool
Conflicts during rebase and cherry-pick; rerere
Recovering lost commits, fixing a bad merge, splitting and squashing commits
Team exercise: four people, one repository, deliberate conflicts

units.title: Automated testing
topics: Unit, integration and end-to-end tests; the testing pyramid; test runners for Python, JavaScript and Java
Linting and formatting as automated checks; pre-commit hooks
Code coverage and its limits; flaky tests
Test-driven development in a small kata

units.title: Continuous integration pipelines
topics: CI principles: every push builds and tests; fast feedback; the build must stay green
GitHub Actions: workflows, jobs, steps, matrices, caching, secrets; GitLab CI compared
Pipeline stages: lint, test, build, package, publish artefacts
Status checks on pull requests; badges; notifications
Reproducible builds and dependency pinning; software supply-chain basics

units.title: Containers
topics: Why containers: environment drift; images versus containers; namespaces and cgroups in brief
Docker: Dockerfile, layers, build, run, volumes, networks, environment variables
Multi-stage builds and small images; registries and tagging
Docker Compose for an app with a database and a cache
Introduction to Kubernetes: pods, deployments, services; when it is overkill

units.title: Automated deployment
topics: Environments: development, staging, production; configuration and secrets management
Deploying a web app to a VPS, a PaaS and a static host from CI; infrastructure as code with Terraform or Ansible in brief
Deployment strategies: rolling, blue-green, canary; database migrations
Continuous delivery versus continuous deployment; release gates and approvals

units.title: Monitoring and rollback
topics: Logs, metrics and traces; structured logging; Prometheus and Grafana or a hosted equivalent
Health checks, uptime monitoring, alerting and on-call basics
Service level indicators and objectives; error budgets
Rolling back a bad release: image tags, reverting commits, feature flags; blameless post-mortems

units.title: DevOps culture and capstone
topics: The DORA metrics: deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, time to restore
DevSecOps: dependency scanning, secret scanning, container scanning in the pipeline
Capstone: take a small application from repository to monitored deployment with a full pipeline
Working with low bandwidth: shallow clones, partial clones, caching, offline-first workflows
